answer: Each identity registers one grove bed and locks a 70-credit bond, paying a fee starting at 28 credits, rising by 5 per earlier bed, so the 1,000th bed pays 5,023 and 1,000 fake beds pay 2,525,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. Each epoch the bed sends a signed signal reporting saffron shoots; an auditor recounts them against the grove ledger and burns the bond if the count is off by more than two or one shoot tag appears on two beds. A rented-shoot ring fails because moved shoots carry their bed tag, exposing the double listing. An honest grower pays 28 once and keeps one bed.
